articles.title: KPop Demon Hunters on 4K Blu-ray costs less than a month of Netflix Premium
articles.summary: The 4K Criterion Collection set is available to pick up at Barnes and Noble for $25.
articles.body: Buying the 4K Blu-ray disc version of KPop Demon Hunters was already going to be a wise idea for some people, especially those who primarily keep their $26.99 Netflix Premium subscription just to watch the hit animated flick in 4K. But at just $24.99 from Barnes and Noble instead of its original $49.95 price, it’s easier than ever to recommend. One important thing to note: it’s unavailable to ship from Barnes and Noble, but you can find a discounted copy at most retail stores, and the site makes it easy to reserve a copy online to pick up later. Amazon was matching the price earlier today, but is currently offering a slightly less tempting deal. [Product: KPop Demon Hunters (4K Blu-ray) | The Criterion Collection version of the film recently launched, and comes with a bunch of extras in a gorgeous set. In addition to the 4K digital master, complete with Dolby Vision HDR and Dolby Atmos sound, you also get two standard 1080p Blu-rays, one containing the film, and the other packed with special features (a full feature-length animatic, a making-of documentary, lyric videos, and more). It includes physical goodies, too, like collectible postcards, as well as an essay by Polygon alum Karen Han. Kpop Demon Hunters was on my list of physical movies to buy, and this deal just turned it into a must-buy ahead of the holiday season.

articles.title: This see-through camera lets photographers maintain eye contact with their subjects
articles.summary: The HOA A1 is a digital camera that incorporates a large viewfinder into its design so photographers can look at what they’re framing instead of a screen.
articles.body: Lutra, a South Korean startup, has debuted a new brand called Humans of Authenticity (HOA) that’s launching another screen-free digital camera that incorporates a large open viewfinder into its design, as spotted by PetaPixel. The camera is reminiscent of the Godox C100 but the HOA A1 positions its lens and sensor close to the center of its large viewfinder window so that a photographer can maintain eye contact with their subject, or feel more in the moment while framing a shot without staring at a screen. The HOA A1 First Edition is expected to launch on December 1st in a very limited run of just 100 units. Preorders haven’t started yet, but the camera will be priced at 360,000 South Korean won, or $289 for US customers. The A1 features a 16-megapixel, 1/2.53-inch Sony sensor paired with a 26mm f/1.75 lens. There is a tiny LCD display on the back but it’s used to display information like battery life and your remaining shots. Everything else about the camera is strictly point and shoot with a shutter button located on its top edge. [Image: The HOA website doesn’t include extensive details about the camera’s capabilities, or even sample shots captured by the A1. According to the site the company is still “fine-tuning the camera’s color and tone in collaboration with photographers.” It does confirm that instead of copying photos to a device or PC using a USB cable or by removing a memory card, the A1 connects to Wi-Fi and wirelessly makes your shots available by tapping your smartphone to the back of the camera. A wireless connection to the internet isn’t needed to take photos, but you’ll need access to Wi-Fi to view and download your shots. The A1 uses a system called ShootProof that authenticates every image captured with an anonymous certificate recorded to a public blockchain. That feature doesn’t appear optional, but there’s also a signature mode you can turn on or off that lets you sign your name in an accompanying app and then have it overlaid in the corner of every photo.

articles.title: Meta’s refurbished Quest 3S headset is nearly $100 off right now
articles.summary: Meta’s refurbished Quest 3S headset is on sale for just $255.99 on eBay right now. You can also save on a Philips Hue lightstrip and Anker’s Desktop USB-C Hub.
articles.body: If you’re curious about virtual reality, Meta’s Quest 3S is a good entry-level headset for dipping your toes in, especially now it’s on sale in refurbished condition for $255.99 directly from Meta’s eBay storefront through November 8th when you use coupon code SAVE20TECH. For comparison, the headset recently dropped to $300 in new condition as part of Amazon’s fall Prime Day event, and currently retails for $349.99. According to eBay, the certified refurbished headset is in “like-new” condition and has undergone professional inspection and cleaning by the manufacturer. More importantly, it comes with either original or new accessories — including a power adapter, a glasses spacer, wrist straps, etc. — alongside a two-year Allstate warranty. [Product: Meta Quest 3S | The Quest 3S strikes a middle ground between the Quest 3 and Quest 2. Like the pricier Quest 3, it runs on the speedy Snapdragon XR2 Gen 2 chip and supports the same library of games. It also comes with the same cameras for full-color passthrough, letting you interact with the world around you while wearing the headset. It comes with Meta’s Touch Plus controllers, though you can also use your hands to navigate menus and interact with some apps. And because it’s a standalone headset, you don’t need a PC or console to play games. However, its display resolution and optics quality are closer to the Quest 2’s, which, while good, means visuals are narrower and less sharp. Still, as we noted in our review, those trade-offs are easy to overlook given the price, especially if you’re new to VR. Read our full Meta Quest 3S review. Three more deals worth a look * Philips Hue’s 80-inch Gradient Lightstrip is on sale for $83.16 ($115 off) when you buy it directly from Philips’ online storefront with code OUTLET58. The two-meter lightstrip can extend up to 10 meters and display multiple colors simultaneously, while delivering up to 1,800 lumens of brightness with customizable lighting effects. You can also control it via Alexa and Google Assistant, or using either Bluetooth or a Philips Hue Bridge. * Anker’s new Desktop USB-C Hub is currently available from both Amazon and Anker (with code WSPDV2ONVYED) for $79.99 ($20 off), which is $5 shy of its lowest price to date. The 10-in-1 hub features a built-in screen that not only displays charging speeds, but also doubles as a digital photo frame and customizable timer. It also sports an HDMI port, a DisplayPort connection, four USB ports, an ethernet jack, and SD and microSD card slots, letting you connect multiple accessories and external displays. * Speaking of gadgets with personality, Orico’s adorable PixCharge Plus is on sale at Amazon in several colors for $29.99 ($50 off), its best price to date. The small, 10,000mAh power bank has a customizable 16-by-16 pixel screen that displays animations, scrolling text, and pixel art using a companion app; it also supports up to 22.5W fast-charging and comes with a built-in USB-C cable that conveniently doubles as a strap.

articles.title: The iPhone Duo has more than 100,000 optimized apps, Apple says
articles.summary: Even though a lot of apps have been updated for the iPhone Duo, they sometimes still have issues.
articles.body: Apple’s iPhone Duo has been officially on sale for two weeks, and the company said today that the App Store now has over 100,000 apps that are built for the foldable. “It’s been wonderful to see how quickly developers have embraced iPhone Duo, and we’re grateful for their creativity and innovation,” Susan Prescott, Apple’s VP of Worldwide Developer Relations, says in a statement. “Today there are well over 100,000 apps built for iPhone Duo already live on the App Store, and thousands of optimized apps are being added to the store each day.” Prescott adds that “the enthusiasm has been incredible, and we’re excited to see the pace of updates continue to accelerate as more and more apps optimize for iPhone Duo.” Although there are now many apps that are optimized for the Duo, they can sometimes still have some issues. When the Duo launched, users noted that the Instagram app was a little messy even though Apple gave it the “Made for iPhone Duo” label, and Instagram chief Adam Mosseri called the Duo a “bit of a tricky form factor.”

articles.title: Kobo will soon let you upload and sync your own ebooks across devices, for a price
articles.summary: Kobo’s new Stack subscription service syncs your own ebooks and PDFs between your e-readers and apps.
articles.body: Kobo is launching a new monthly subscription service called Stack that lets you upload your own ebooks and documents to the company’s servers where they’ll be synced across multiple devices and apps, including your reading progress, highlights, and annotations. Kobo Stack is similar to Amazon’s Send to Kindle feature that allows users to upload a wide variety of files to their Kindle libraries for free, but Kobo’s version will cost a few dollars each month. Kobo Stack is being introduced as part of a major 6.0 update to the company’s e-reader software, which is available in beta now as an optional upgrade ahead of a wider official release. Supported document types include EPUBs and PDFs up to 200MB in size and files can be pushed to Kobo Cloud using a drag and drop interface on the company’s website, or by emailing them to a custom address you get when you subscribe to Stack. Your uploaded documents are synced and available anywhere you’re logged in to your Kobo account, including the iOS and Android apps, the Kobo website, and the company’s e-readers. Kobo Stack’s e-reader support is currently limited to recent devices including the Clara BW, Clara Colour, Libra Colour, and the Elipsa 2E, but access for older devices “made between 2018 and 2024 will arrive soon,” according to Kobo’s website. The initial rollout of Kobo Stack is limited to Canada, Ireland, Australia, New Zealand, the UK, and Spain, according to details Kobo CEO Michael Tamblyn shared on Threads, but not the US. Canadian pricing is $3.99 per month, while in the UK it’s £2.99 per month. Kobo is offering a free 90-day trial for those wanting to test it out, and there’s a 60-day grace period if you choose to cancel your subscription. That gives you around two months to download and back up any files you’ve uploaded, and to export your notes and annotations. After 60 days, everything will be permanently deleted. Other features being introduced as part of the new Kobo firmware update include the ability to add multiple library cards so you can borrow books from several libraries through Libby, lower stylus latency on devices with pen support, improved accessibility with even larger font options, and support for EPUB files protected by LCP DRM.

This version is meant as a more budget-friendly variant for content creators looking for a simpler setup, with both an XLR output and USB-C, letting you wire into an audio interface or directly to a computer.

articles.title: Felicity Porter is messy, earnest and a little cringe. Her Gen Z fans are here for it.
articles.summary: For all her quirks and flaws and rash decisions, Felicity keeps learning to trust herself. It’s another reason Gen Z viewers feel connected to her.
articles.body:
In the final moments of the Felicity pilot, Felicity Porter (Keri Russell) is having dinner with her parents at a fancy restaurant in New York City. Convinced she's made a grave mistake by moving to the Big Apple on a whim, her parents urge — and even try to bribe — her to return home to Palo Alto, Calif., and pursue medicine as planned. Felicity is quiet, seemingly weighing her options in real time before mustering the courage to speak. "I guess the thing is," she begins. "That if I made a mistake… then at least it was mine, you know?"

The scene is short but pivotal — and captures the essence of the show. Created by J.J. Abrams and Matt Reeves, Felicity , which ran from 1998 to 2002, is a coming-of-age series about a soft-spoken teen who derails her college plans after one conversation with her longtime crush. The series has found a new generation of fans since arriving on Netflix in October.

After speaking to Ben Covington (Scott Speedman) for the first time at their high school graduation, Felicity abandons her plans to attend Stanford and instead follows him across the country to the (fictional) University of New York. Does she have a clue what she's doing? Hardly. For many first-time Gen Z viewers, her decision to prioritize a guy is pretty cringe.

New Felicity fans have criticized the Palo Alto teen for being " insane ," " delusional " and " a lil too embarrassing " — despite having "endearing and cute mannerisms." Viewers have also made some sweeping condemnations, declaring Felicity is " worse than Carrie Bradshaw " and the show itself " a humiliation ritual. "

And yet, Felicity has managed to captivate this wave of new, younger viewers anyway, emerging as something of an inspiration — however unhinged she may be.

"A lot of it is just the everyday struggles of a college girl figuring out her life, rather than the over-the-top, sometimes unrealistic high school and college dramas we see today," Alexa, 28, told Yahoo. "I think there's something really nice about watching a show where the little things in life are enough to make a story interesting."

Felicity demonstrates just how willing she is to put herself out there — and how in tune she is with her own feelings over the course of the series. Is it kind of rash to follow someone you have a crush on to college? Absolutely. But that's what makes her so compelling to younger audiences: She does the big, scary thing.

Camila, 28, told Yahoo that while some of Felicity's decisions have "definitely" been "a hard watch," she understands them. "Personally, I've done some questionable things when having a crush on someone," she said. "I think that aspect resonates a lot with people."

Shadon, 25, said Felicity's vulnerability is what drew her to the character. There's something to be said about a young woman who goes after what she wants regardless of what anyone thinks.

"A lesson I learned from Felicity herself is that it's OK to be honest about how I'm feeling," she told Yahoo. "So many characters in the modern landscape hold back how they really feel to keep up a certain facade, but Felicity is always willing to put it all out there."

Her willingness to go after what she wants extends beyond romance. Ben might have been the reason she moved to New York — but he isn't why she stayed. "Felicity has definitely taught me to follow my heart more," Chelsea, 25, told Yahoo. "It might not always work out but I think you can learn a lot about yourself when leading with your heart rather than your head all the time. Moving to New York quickly became so much bigger than chasing some boy."

She also isn't afraid to defy her parents. Felicity's career path has been mapped out for as long as she can remember — graduate high school, attend Stanford as a premed student, continue on to medical school and so on — but it wasn't what she wanted. Not immediately, anyway. She needed the space to figure things out.

"I really enjoyed how much emphasis the show put on her not having her life plan figured out, even when she was in her last year of college," Shadon added. "Felicity was constantly shown changing career paths and having no idea of what she wanted to do once she graduated, which I could definitely relate to."

Davey Chafe, a clinical psychologist, told Yahoo that Felicity's desire for independence reflects a process known as separation and individuation , which happens during late adolescence and early adulthood. It's essentially a period of flux.

"It's basically when we are learning who we are outside of our family and our caregivers, so our main family unit," Chafe said. Felicity even articulates the lack of control she's had over her own life when the show begins. She notes early on that her dad was "thrilled" she got into Stanford because he "had my life planned out for me since I was pretty much a zygote."

"Especially at that age, the decisions we're making during that period are really driven a bit more by emotion and kind of trial and error than logic," Chafe said. "I think that's a pretty accurate reflection of what growing up can feel like."

Maria DiPasquale, a longtime Felicity fan and founder of Leftist Teen Drama , a podcast that celebrates political moments in teen TV, cites a Season 2 storyline as one of the show's most important.

In "Revolutions," the season's 16th episode, Felicity helps stage a sit-in at the student health center after learning the university's board of trustees has banned the morning-after pill. Despite mounting pressure from the school to stand down, she forges ahead with the days-long protest. The board eventually reverses its ban after Julie (Amy Jo Johnson), Felicity's best friend, reveals she used the pill after being sexually assaulted on campus.

When a television show makes a concerted effort to spotlight political issues that affect young people, DiPasquale told Yahoo, she's "gonna give them their flowers." She hopes the episode encourages new viewers to take action in their communities.

"I think it's a really timeless message," she said. "I really hope that young people are inspired by the plot line and realize that they also have the power to do what Felicity and her friends do and they can win. Any injustice on your campus, in your school, in your workplace — you have the power in working with other people, with other students, to put your heads together and figure out how you can make injustice go away."

As a younger millennial, watching Felicity makes me feel as though I've been transported to a completely different time. Felicity swears by her tape recorder, which we see her use in the show's opening minutes. She goes to the library to conduct research for her college papers. She runs to pay phones to make urgent calls and even leaves her dorm room to have face-to-face conversations with other people.

There's an instant gratification that social media and modern technology afford us — an immediacy that didn't exist in the 1990s. Felicity, for instance, is someone who sits in her feelings a lot. I can't imagine that'd be as easy if she had Instagram at her fingertips.

"There's something really comforting about watching relationships unfold where people aren't constantly accessible to one another. I think that it just gives people a little more space, right? Which you can feel in the show," Chafe said. "I think for younger people, part of the comfort is seeing everyone navigate the awkwardness, uncertainty and intensity of growing up without feeling like every moment is being watched."

The show's analog, pre-social media existence is something Gen Z viewers yearn for. Chelsea told Yahoo that "it is so rare to see someone be so completely free" in the age of social media. Now, she said, "we are all desperate to appear polished and we put on personas to appear cooler on the internet."

"It's refreshing to see a version of college life that's still so relatable to what we experience today, but without phones and social media being such a big part of it," Alexa said. "It almost feels like an escape, especially now that technology and social media seem to find their way into every show we watch."

Chafe hopes Felicity will inspire younger audiences to spend more time offline. "We've never been more connected but also never been more lonely," he said. "If people are connecting to the show there's a reason, and I think part of the reason is that it does feel a bit more human."

For all her quirks and flaws and rash decisions, Felicity keeps learning to trust herself. That's not to say she hasn't considered stifling her own wants to appease others, but her struggle to prioritize her feelings is part of what makes her so relatable. It's another reason Gen Z viewers feel connected to her: She gives main-character energy.

"Felicity lives her life like she's the main character, and personally, I think that's how everyone should live," Alexa said. "I think there's something really refreshing about watching someone who isn't afraid to take herself and her feelings seriously, even if it makes her look ridiculous sometimes."

At a time when social media makes it easier to hide what we're actually feeling, Felicity reminds us there's merit in being exactly who you are, regardless of what anyone thinks. There's something deeply human about her hesitation and fear of hurting others, even as she finds the courage to put herself first. Perhaps there's something to be said about being a little bit cringe and taking a chance: It could be worth it in the long run.

articles.title: ‘Dirty Sanchez’ star Mike Locke passes away at age 47
articles.summary: Mike Locke, beloved Welsh stuntman and TV personality known for ‘Dirty Sanchez,’ has passed away at the age of 47, leaving a legacy of laughter and friendship.
articles.body: Mike Locke has passed away. He was a Welsh stuntman, skateboarder, and television personality best known for co-starring in MTV UK's Gonzo stunt show, ‘Dirty Sanchez.' Best known by his nickname, Pancho, Locke was a beloved member of the community.Mike Locke passes awayMike Locke’s death news was confirmed through San Portablo's (his brand's) Instagram on Friday morning, November 6, which talked about the artist and the impact he left on the people around him. The post wrote about him, calling Locke "an absolute Welsh treasure" and "all-round goodfellow" who "lit up the world with his charm."The entire post read, "An absolute Welsh treasure and San Portablo King. His brilliance, we are sure, will still shine through far, wide, high, and low and across the seven seas. He lived an incredible life and lit up the world with his charm. Rest in peace, brother; your legend will never cease. It will only gain momentum.”BBC reported on a video from Matthew Pritchard, a fellow TV star from ‘Dirty Sanchez,' talking about Mike Locke inside them. He shared, “I'm still a little bit in shock. My little friend of more than 35 years has left the building. We've had some amazing laughs together over the years. I've known him since he was about 14 years old. Of course the Sanchez years, travelling all over the world with him, having been in some classic messes with him in the past, partying. Now he's gone, but I'll never forget him.”Fellow TV star Lee Dainton also wrote on social media, saying, "When you grow up skating with your friends, you're in your own little world. You never think about losing anyone from it. In your head those days and the people you shared them with live forever. Since hearing the news all those memories have been flooding back. I can see Panch, hear the laughter, and remember all the best times like they were yesterday. Then it hits me that he's gone, and I still can't believe it.” He shared the statement along with a long carousel of their photos together.Sando Ford also took to his Instagram account to share his condolences, saying, “People might know him from the TV stuff, but he was much more than that; he was a clever, hilarious, and loyal person,” Ford wrote. “He would … travel to open mics with me just to watch me die on my ass and laugh about it on the way home.”Mike Locke was born on March 13, 1979, in Neath, Wales, and was best known for his work on ‘Dirty Sanchez.' He also appeared in the TV show 'Balls of Steel,' as well as 'Death Wish Live.' At the time of writing, no official cause of his death has been shared with the public.Get the latest TV News, TV Shows and more. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Sa Re Ga Ma Pa Tamil: Former chorus singer Jovin Jonix gets selected, says 'I used to sit with the other contestants and sing in the chorus'
articles.summary: In the latest episode of Sa Re Ga Ma Pa Tamil, a contestant's long-awaited opportunity to showcase his talent turned into an emotional moment.
articles.body: In the latest episode of Sa Re Ga Ma Pa Tamil, a contestant's long-awaited opportunity to showcase his talent turned into an emotional moment. Jovin Jonix, who once appeared on the show's stage as a chorus singer in Season 3, finally got the chance to stand before the judges as a contestant. His journey and determination caught judge Srinivas's attention, and he had words of encouragement for the aspiring singer before selecting him for the competition.After hearing Jovin's performance, Srinivas wanted to know more about him and asked about his background. Jovin opened up about his musical journey and the challenges he had faced along the way. "I'm from Kanyakumari. I came to Chennai in 2019. I kept trying, and during Season 3, I was right here at this very place. I used to sit with the other contestants and sing in the chorus. From there, I've come a little further. I kept pushing myself, telling myself not to give up, and now I'm finally standing on this stage. All these years that I've been running towards my dream, my family has been running right alongside me," he said.Impressed by his story, Srinivas went on to appreciate Jovin's potential as a singer. "I like you, man. As a personality, I like you. And I feel you have such a beautiful voice. If you get the right sound choice and proper training, you can rock the stage," he told him.The moment became even more special when Srinivas pressed the selection button, giving Jovin the opportunity to move forward in the competition. Overwhelmed by the development, Jovin and his family were seen getting emotional. The stage also erupted in applause as everyone celebrated his selection.For Jovin, it was a major milestone in his musical journey. He had once stood on the same stage as a chorus singer, and now he finally had the chance to showcase his individual talent before the judges. Going from being a chorus singer in Season 3 to a selected contestant made the moment all the more special.Meanwhile, Sa Re Ga Ma Pa Seniors Season 6 continues to provide aspiring singers with a platform to showcase their talent, with Srinivas, Vijay Prakash, S. P. Charan and Shweta Mohan as judges and Archana Chandhoke as the host.Get the latest TV News, TV Shows and more. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Kaun Banega Crorepati 18 shoot halted for a week amid Amitabh Bachchan’s health concerns, channel to air old episodes
articles.summary: Legendary star Amitabh Bachchan returned to television in August with his iconic game quiz show, Kaun Banega Crorepati 18.
articles.body: Legendary star Amitabh Bachchan returned to television in August with his iconic game quiz show, Kaun Banega Crorepati 18. The megastar, who has been entertaining the audience with his hosting skills even at the age of 84, is not keeping well. As per a report in IANS, the shoot of Amitabh Bachchan’s popular quiz show “Kaun Banega Crorepati” has been halted for the past one week owing to the actor’s health concerns.A source informed the news agency that the legendary actor has not been keeping well and the makers have temporarily stopped filming new episodes. In the meantime, the channel has been re-airing a few week-old episodes featuring celebrity guests as part of its Diwali special week.The source revealed that the last major celebrity episode shot for the show featured Ranbir Kapoor, Sai Pallavi and Ravi Dubey, who appeared on the quiz show to promote their upcoming film “Ramayana”.The source further went on to share that the episode featuring the “Ramayan” cast was originally planned to coincide with the film’s release. However, owing to the megastar’s health concerns, the entire plan had to be reworked. Instead of holding the episode back for the film’s release, the channel began the Diwali special week last week with the “Ramayan” episode.The shoot is expected to resume from next week now, if Big B feels well. "The shoot will resume hopefully from next week but only if his health allows," said the source further.Amitabh Bachchan, who has been hosting Kaun Banega Crorepati for several seasons, reflected on returning to his daily routine and shared his thoughts on his bond with well-wishers in his latest blog post on Saturday.“... and the gentle but slow return to routine and the controlled life... OF WORK... and the others. When in routine you remember the routine... when not... even routine develops a temperament .. not explainable .. and never the same...” Amitabh wrote.He added, “Oh ! where did I leave my glasses .. the mobile .. and most importantly .. what was I supposed to do next... the deeds and acts done just a couple of hours ago .. lost in oblivion .. but what Class 8 was like in School 1960 at your finger-tips .. 66 years at the back of your hand .. and now .. a searching! But ..”“Never a searching for the connect on Blog .. that be the preference .. each day... nor, the well wishers of each Sunday... nor, the KBC audience , who extend love affection and the sincerity of their warmth and endearing presence... my prayers for all.”The veteran actor’s health has remained a matter of concern for his fans, with Amitabh Bachchan’s well-being being closely followed over the years.Amitabh Bachchan’s history with health scares also dates back to one of the most traumatic incidents of his career, during his near-fatal accident on the sets of “Coolie” in 1982.During a fight sequence with actor Puneet Issar, a mistimed blow resulted in a major abdominal injury, leaving the legend fighting for his life. He was reportedly declared clinically dead for a few minutes and underwent multiple surgeries.The incident triggered a humongous wave of concern across the country, within millions of fans praying for his recovery.Amitabh Bachchan has repeatedly expressed gratitude for those prayers and has described August 2, the day he returned home after the accident, as his “second birthday”. He has always credited the prayers and affection of his fans with giving him another chance at life.Get the latest TV News, TV Shows and more. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Costco members can get $5 off the reimagined Ocarina of Time
articles.summary: Costco members can purchase the digital version of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time for $55, a $5 discount on the Switch 2 game’s MSRP.
articles.body: While some retailers were offering preorder discounts on the remastered Legend of Zelda: The Ocarina of Time, it’s not too late to save if you missed out. Costco members can currently get $5 off the digital version online, bringing the price down to $54.99. Considering an annual Costco membership runs $65, that discount almost offsets one month of your plan — a prime example of “gamer math.” [Product: The Legend of Zelda: The Ocarina of Time | My colleague Andrew Webster recently shared his thoughts on Nintendo’s latest Switch 2 exclusive, noting how impressed he was with how much impact a few modern quality-of-life changes had on what is otherwise a classic experience. The updated graphics are as thoughtful as they are beautiful, pairing realistic scenery with puppet-like characters. Perhaps, more importantly, Link can now jump anytime he likes, rather than being limited to specific ledges.
